newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: More Afghan refugees flee to Kabul from frontline.
newsitem.headline: More Afghan refugees flee to Kabul from frontline.

text.p: More than 30,000 refugees have flooded into the Afghan capital Kabul over the past five days, fleeing from frontlines in fighting to the north of the city, a United Nations report said on Wednesday.

"Yesterday alone, almost 10,000 displaced people entered Kabul, taking the total number of those who have arrived...since January 2 to 67,000," a statement by the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees said.
The report, released at an International Forum on Assistance to Afghanistan taking place in Turkmenistan's capital of Ashgabat, said 31,000 people had fled to Kabul in five days.
It said the influx was caused by the fall of the town of Charikar, some 50 km (30 miles) north of Kabul, on January 16.
The Taleban Islamic militia seized Charikar and the nearby Bagram military air base last Thursday in a lightening offensive against forces loyal to general Abdul Rashid Dostum and Ahmad Shah Masood.
The Taleban captured the same territory soon after seizing Kabul in September but lost it after Masood, military commander in the ousted government, hit back with guerrilla tactics.
"Most of Kabul's inhabitants are desperately poor and their capacity to absorb tens of thousands of displaced persons may be very limited," the report said.
